newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn to develop Las Vegas complex.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn to develop Las Vegas complex.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp on Thursday said it had signed an agreement to develop a 450,000 square foot retail and entertainment complex in Las Vegas.
The value of the deal was not disclosed.

The new complex is part of the overall redevelopment of the Aladdin Hotel and Casino. TrizecHahn said it signed the agreement with Aladdin Holdings LLC, which is controlled by the Sommer family of Las Vegas and New York.

The new shopping center is part of the overal l redevelopment of the Aladdin Hotel and Casino. TrizecHahn said it signed the agreement with Aladdin Holdings LLC, which is controlled by the Sommer family of Las Vegas and New York.

The new complex will be known as the Aladdin Shopping Center and will be designed to complement the overall theme of the redeveloped hotel and casino. TrizecHahn's retail division, TrizecHahn Centers will develop, lease and operate the new mall.

TrizecHahn spokeswoman Laurie Ludwick told Reuters the project cost of the retail complex will be about US$200 million, while the cost of the overall Aladdin redevelopment including the shopping center will be about US$600 million.
The company said it expects the redevelopment of the Aladdin and the construction of the retail center to begin later this year, with the center scheduled to open in 1999.

TrizecHahn executive vice president Lee Wagman said in a statement that the center will be well located on the Las Vegas Strip and will benefit from a huge volume of pedestrian and automobile traffic.

Based in Toronto, TrizecHahn is one of North America's largest publicly traded real estate companies. The company's shares were down C$0.10 to C$30.80 in midafternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
